transcription.tex: Use vectors to represent motion. Can we use the \(suvat\) equations with constant acceleration? What changes when acceleration varies with time \(t\)?

\textbf{1. Vector equations for motion}\par A particle has velocity\[\mathbf v=(1-2t)\mathbf i+(3t-3)\mathbf j\quad\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}.\]Find (a) its speed at \(t=0\); (b) its bearing at \(t=2\); (c) when it moves (i) parallel to \(\mathbf j\), (ii) parallel to \(-\mathbf i-3\mathbf j\). (3, 2, 6 marks)

\textbf{2. Variable acceleration with vectors}\par A particle \(P\), mass \(0.8\,\mathrm{kg}\), is acted on by a single force \(\mathbf F\). Its position relative to fixed origin \(O\) is\[\mathbf r=2t^3\mathbf i+50t^{-1/2}\mathbf j\quad\mathrm m,\quad t>0.\]Find (a) its speed at \(t=4\); (b) acceleration as a vector at \(t=2\); (c) \(\mathbf F\) at \(t=2\).

\textbf{3. Integration for velocity/displacement}\par A particle moving in a plane has velocity\[\mathbf v=3t\mathbf i+\tfrac12t^2\mathbf j\quad\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}},\quad t\geq0.\]At \(t=0\), its position relative to \(O\) is \((2\mathbf i-3\mathbf j)\,\mathrm m\). Find its position vector at time \(t\).

transcription.tex: Initially, a ball has position vector \(\binom31\,\mathrm m\). Each second it moves by \(\binom42\,\mathrm m\): its constant velocity is \(\binom42\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\).\par Where is it after 1 second? After 2 seconds?
After 1 second:\[\binom31+\binom42=\binom73\,\mathrm m.\]
After 2 seconds:\[\binom31+2\binom42=\binom{11}5\,\mathrm m.\]
In general, where is the ball after t seconds?
Add \(t\) lots of \(\binom42\) to \(\binom31\):\[\binom31+t\binom42=\binom{3+4t}{1+2t}.\]
\textbf{Position vector}\[\mathbf r=\mathbf r_0+\mathbf vt,\]where \(\mathbf r_0\) is initial position and \(\mathbf v\) is constant velocity.

transcription.tex: A particle starts at \((3\mathbf i+7\mathbf j)\,\mathrm m\), moving with constant velocity \((2\mathbf i-\mathbf j)\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\).\par (a) Find its position vector 4 seconds later.\par (b) Find when it is due east of the origin.
\[\mathbf r=\binom37+4\binom2{-1}=\binom{11}3\,\mathrm m.\]

Due east means the \(\mathbf j\) component is zero and the \(\mathbf i\) component is positive:\[\mathbf r=\binom37+t\binom2{-1}=\binom{3+2t}{7-t}.\]\[7-t=0\quad\Rightarrow\quad t=7\,\mathrm s.\]The east component is then \(17\,\mathrm m>0\).
Column vectors may be easier to manipulate than i and j notation; either may be used.

transcription.tex: Some \(suvat\) equations work with vectors. Here \(\mathbf r\) denotes displacement from the initial position:\[\mathbf r=\mathbf ut+\tfrac12\mathbf at^2,\qquad\mathbf v=\mathbf u+\mathbf at.\]Which quantities are vectors, and which are scalars?
\(\mathbf r\): vector.
\(\mathbf u\): vector.
\(\mathbf v\): vector.
\(\mathbf a\): vector.
\(t\): scalar. The scalar formula \(v^2=u^2+2as\) cannot be used by simply squaring vector symbols.

A particle has initial velocity \((-3\mathbf i+\mathbf j)\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) and constant acceleration \((2\mathbf i+3\mathbf j)\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\). Find (a) its speed and (b) its bearing at \(t=3\,\mathrm s\).

\[\mathbf v=\mathbf u+\mathbf at\]\[=\binom{-3}1+3\binom23=\binom3{10}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}.\]\[\text{Speed}=\sqrt{3^2+10^2}=10.4\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\quad(3\text{ s.f.}).\]Speed is the scalar magnitude of velocity.
\[\tan\theta=\frac3{10}\Rightarrow\theta=16.7^\circ.\]The bearing is \(017^\circ\). The velocity vector gives the direction of motion; draw it to establish the angle.

transcription.tex: An ice skater is at fixed point \(O\) at \(t=0\), with velocity \((2.4\mathbf i-0.6\mathbf j)\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). At \(t=20\,\mathrm s\), velocity is \((-5.6\mathbf i+3.4\mathbf j)\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Model the skater as a particle with constant acceleration. Find (a) acceleration; (b) position \(\mathbf s\) relative to \(O\) at time \(t\); (c) when directly north-east of \(O\). A second skater has position \(\mathbf r=(1.1t-6)\mathbf j\,\mathrm m\). (d) Show that they meet.
\[\mathbf v=\mathbf u+\mathbf at\]\[\binom{-5.6}{3.4}=\binom{2.4}{-0.6}+20\mathbf a\]\[20\mathbf a=\binom{-8}4\]\[\mathbf a=\binom{-0.4}{0.2}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}.\]
\[\mathbf s=\mathbf ut+\tfrac12\mathbf at^2\]\[=\binom{2.4}{-0.6}t+\tfrac12\binom{-0.4}{0.2}t^2\]\[=\binom{2.4t-0.2t^2}{-0.6t+0.1t^2}\,\mathrm m.\]

North-east: equal positive components.\[2.4t-0.2t^2=-0.6t+0.1t^2\]\[3t(1-0.1t)=0\]\[t=0\quad\text{or}\quad t=10.\]Reject \(t=0\), at the origin. At \(t=10\), both components are 4, so the time is \(10\,\mathrm s\).

Meeting requires equal position vectors:\[\binom{2.4t-0.2t^2}{-0.6t+0.1t^2}=\binom0{1.1t-6}.\]\[2.4t-0.2t^2=0\]\[0.2t(12-t)=0\Rightarrow t=0\text{ or }12.\]At \(t=0\), north components are \(0\) and \(-6\): no meeting. At \(t=12\):\[-0.6(12)+0.1(12^2)=7.2,\]\[1.1(12)-6=7.2.\]They meet at \(t=12\,\mathrm s\).

transcription.tex: Edexcel M1 (Old), May 2013(R), Q6\par Unit vectors \(\mathbf i,\mathbf j\) point east and north. Ship \(S\) has constant velocity \((3\mathbf i+3\mathbf j)\,\mathrm{km\,h^{-1}}\); at \(t=0\), position is \((-4\mathbf i+2\mathbf j)\,\mathrm{km}\). (a) Find its position at time \(t\) hours. Ship \(T\) has velocity \((-2\mathbf i+n\mathbf j)\,\mathrm{km\,h^{-1}}\), initial position \((6\mathbf i+\mathbf j)\,\mathrm{km}\). They meet at \(P\). (b) Find \(n\). (c) Find \(OP\). (2,5,4 marks)
\[\mathbf r=\mathbf r_0+\mathbf vt\]\[=(-4\mathbf i+2\mathbf j)+(3\mathbf i+3\mathbf j)t\]\[=(-4+3t)\mathbf i+(2+3t)\mathbf j.\]

For ship \(T\):\[\mathbf r_T=(6\mathbf i+\mathbf j)+(-2\mathbf i+n\mathbf j)t\]\[=(6-2t)\mathbf i+(1+nt)\mathbf j.\]At meeting, positions are identical:\[-4+3t=6-2t\]\[5t=10\Rightarrow t=2.\]\[2+3(2)=1+2n\Rightarrow n=3.5.\]
At \(t=2\), position of \(P\):\[(-4+6)\mathbf i+(2+6)\mathbf j=2\mathbf i+8\mathbf j.\]\[OP=\sqrt{2^2+8^2}\]\[=\sqrt{68}=8.25\,\mathrm{km}\]\[(3\text{ s.f.}).\]

transcription.tex: 10. A model boat has constant acceleration \((0.2\mathbf i+0.6\mathbf j)\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\). After 20 seconds its velocity is \((4\mathbf i+3\mathbf j)\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Find displacement from its starting position after 20 seconds.

\(\mathbf v=4\mathbf i+3\mathbf j,\ t=20,\ \mathbf a=0.2\mathbf i+0.6\mathbf j\). Find \(\mathbf s\):\[\mathbf s=\mathbf vt-\tfrac12\mathbf at^2\]\[=20(4\mathbf i+3\mathbf j)-\frac{20^2}2(0.2\mathbf i+0.6\mathbf j)\]\[=80\mathbf i+60\mathbf j-40\mathbf i-120\mathbf j\]\[=40\mathbf i-60\mathbf j.\]After 20 seconds, displacement is \((40\mathbf i-60\mathbf j)\,\mathrm m\).

transcription.tex: 11. Particle \(A\) starts at \((12\mathbf i+12\mathbf j)\,\mathrm m\), with velocity \((-\mathbf i+\mathbf j)\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) and constant acceleration \((2\mathbf i-4\mathbf j)\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\). Particle \(B\) has initial velocity \(\mathbf i\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) and constant acceleration \(2\mathbf j\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\). They collide after 3 seconds. Find (a) both speeds then; (b) the collision point’s position vector; (c) \(B\)’s initial position vector.

Use \(\mathbf v=\mathbf u+\mathbf at\), \(t=3\). For \(A\):\[\mathbf v=(-\mathbf i+\mathbf j)+3(2\mathbf i-4\mathbf j)\]\[=(-1+6)\mathbf i+(1-12)\mathbf j\]\[=5\mathbf i-11\mathbf j.\]\[|\mathbf v|=\sqrt{5^2+11^2}\]\[=\sqrt{25+121}=\sqrt{146}\]\[=12.1\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\quad(3\text{ s.f.}).\]For \(B\):\[\mathbf v=\mathbf i+3(2\mathbf j)=\mathbf i+6\mathbf j\]\[|\mathbf v|=\sqrt{1^2+6^2}\]\[=\sqrt{1+36}=\sqrt{37}\]\[=6.08\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\quad(3\text{ s.f.}).\]

For \(A\), \(\mathbf s=\mathbf ut+\tfrac12\mathbf at^2\):\[\mathbf s=3(-\mathbf i+\mathbf j)+\tfrac12(2\mathbf i-4\mathbf j)9\]\[=-3\mathbf i+3\mathbf j+9\mathbf i-18\mathbf j\]\[=6\mathbf i-15\mathbf j.\]At collision:\[\mathbf r=\mathbf r_0+\mathbf s\]\[=(12\mathbf i+12\mathbf j)+(6\mathbf i-15\mathbf j)\]\[=18\mathbf i-3\mathbf j\,\mathrm m.\]

First find \(B\)’s displacement:\[\mathbf s=\mathbf ut+\tfrac12\mathbf at^2\]\[=3\mathbf i+\tfrac12(2\mathbf j)9\]\[=3\mathbf i+9\mathbf j.\]\(\text{Initial position =}\)\par \(\text{final position}-\text{displacement:}\)\[\mathbf r_0=\mathbf r-\mathbf s\]\[=(18\mathbf i-3\mathbf j)-(3\mathbf i+9\mathbf j)\]\[=15\mathbf i-12\mathbf j\,\mathrm m.\]

transcription.tex: 12. A ship is at \(O\) at 12:00, with velocity \((-4\mathbf i+8\mathbf j)\,\mathrm{km\,h^{-1}}\). At 14:00 its velocity is \((-2\mathbf i-6\mathbf j)\,\mathrm{km\,h^{-1}}\). At \(t\) hours after 12:00, \(t\geq0\), its displacement is \(\mathbf s\). Model constant acceleration. Find (a) acceleration; (b) \(\mathbf s(t)\); (c) when directly south-west of \(O\). A second ship has position \(\mathbf r=(40-25t)\mathbf j\,\mathrm{km}\). (d) Find where they meet.

\(\mathbf u=-4\mathbf i+8\mathbf j,\ \mathbf v=-2\mathbf i-6\mathbf j,\ t=2\).\[\mathbf v=\mathbf u+\mathbf at\]\[-2\mathbf i-6\mathbf j=-4\mathbf i+8\mathbf j+2\mathbf a\]\[2\mathbf a=2\mathbf i-14\mathbf j\]\[\mathbf a=\mathbf i-7\mathbf j\quad\mathrm{km\,h^{-2}}.\]
\[\mathbf s=\mathbf ut+\tfrac12\mathbf at^2\]\[=(-4\mathbf i+8\mathbf j)t+\tfrac12(\mathbf i-7\mathbf j)t^2\]\[=(-4t+0.5t^2)\mathbf i+(8t-3.5t^2)\mathbf j\,\mathrm{km}.\]

South-west means equal negative components:\[-4t+0.5t^2=8t-3.5t^2\]\[4t^2=12t\quad\Rightarrow\quad t=0\text{ or }3.\]Reject \(t=0\), at \(O\). At \(t=3\), both components are \(-7.5\). This is 3 hours after 12:00, at 15:00.

At meeting, \(\mathbf r=\mathbf s\). As \(\mathbf r\) has no \(\mathbf i\) component:\[-4t+0.5t^2=0\Rightarrow0.5t^2=4t\Rightarrow t=0\text{ or }8.\]At \(t=0\), positions differ: \(0\ne40\mathbf j\). At \(t=8\):\[\mathbf r=(40-25\times8)\mathbf j=-160\mathbf j,\]\[8(8)-3.5(8^2)=-160.\]They meet 160 km south of \(O\), at position \(-160\mathbf j\,\mathrm{km}\).

transcription.tex: At an air show, an aeroplane passes over a control tower with velocity \((20\mathbf i-100\mathbf j)\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), flying horizontally with constant acceleration \(6\mathbf j\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\). A second plane passes the tower \(t>0\) seconds later, with velocity \((70\mathbf i+40\mathbf j)\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), in a higher horizontal plane with acceleration \(-8\mathbf j\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\). They subsequently pass directly over one another. Find \(t\).

Let the horizontal position at crossing be \(\mathbf r\), and let \(T\) be time since the first plane passed the tower. For the first plane:\[\mathbf u=\binom{20}{-100},\quad\mathbf a=\binom06.\]\[\mathbf r=\mathbf uT+\tfrac12\mathbf aT^2\]\[=\binom{20}{-100}T+\frac{T^2}2\binom06\]\[=\binom{20T}{-100T+3T^2}.\]For the second plane, elapsed time is \(T-t\):\[\mathbf r=\binom{70}{40}(T-t)+\frac{(T-t)^2}2\binom0{-8}\]\[=\binom{70T-70t}{40T-40t-4T^2-4t^2+8Tt}.\]

Equate east components:\[20T=70T-70t\]\[70T-20T=70t\quad\Rightarrow\quad T=\frac75t.\]Equate north components:\[-100T+3T^2=40T-40t-4T^2-4t^2+8Tt\]\[7T^2+4t^2-8Tt=140T-40t.\]Substitute \(T=7t/5\):\[\frac{7\times7^2}{25}t^2+4t^2-\frac{8\times7}5t^2\]\[=\frac{140\times7}5t-40t.\]\[\left(\frac{343}{25}+4-\frac{56}5\right)t^2=(196-40)t\]\[\frac{163}{25}t^2=156t.\]As \(t>0\):\[t=\frac{3900}{163}=23.926\ldots\,\mathrm s\]\[=24\,\mathrm s\quad(2\text{ s.f.}).\]

transcription.tex: A velocity vector gives both direction and magnitude, so can represent projection and subsequent motion.\par A racket strikes a ball at \(A\), position \(20\mathbf j\,\mathrm m\) relative to \(O\). Initial velocity is \((5\mathbf i+8\mathbf j)\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), with \(\mathbf i\) horizontal and \(\mathbf j\) upward. It moves freely under gravity until hitting horizontal ground at \(B\). Find (a) speed after 1.5 seconds; (b) position \(\mathbf r(t)\) relative to \(O\); (c) \(OB\).

\[\mathbf v=\mathbf u+\mathbf at\]\[=\binom58+\binom0{-9.8}t\]\[=\binom5{8-9.8t}.\]At \(t=1.5\):\[\mathbf v=\binom5{-6.7}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}.\]\[|\mathbf v|=\sqrt{5^2+6.7^2}\]\[=8.4\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\]\[(2\text{ s.f.}).\]

Displacement relative to \(A\):\[\mathbf r_A=\mathbf ut+\tfrac12\mathbf at^2\]\[=\binom58t+\tfrac12\binom0{-9.8}t^2\]\[=\binom{5t}{8t-4.9t^2}.\]Position relative to \(O\):\[\mathbf r=\binom0{20}+\binom{5t}{8t-4.9t^2}\]\[=\binom{5t}{8t-4.9t^2+20}\,\mathrm m.\]
At ground level, north/up component is zero:\[8t-4.9t^2+20=0.\]Positive root \(t=2.995\ldots\,\mathrm s\). Horizontal component gives\[OB=5t=15\,\mathrm m\quad(2\text{ s.f.}).\]

transcription.tex: Edexcel M2 (Old), January 2012, Q7\par \(\mathbf i,\mathbf j\) are horizontal and vertical upward unit vectors. A ball is projected from \(O\) on horizontal ground with velocity \((6\mathbf i+12\mathbf j)\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). It passes \(A\) at time \(t\); \(B\) is vertically below \(A\) on the ground, with \(OB=2AB\). Find (a) \(t\); (b) speed \(V\) at \(A\). At another point \(C\), speed is also \(V\). (c) Find time from \(O\) to \(C\). (7,5,3 marks)
Horizontal distance: \(6t\). Vertical height: \(12t-\tfrac12gt^2\).\[2(12t-\tfrac12gt^2)=6t\]\[(24-6)t=gt^2.\]As \(t>0\):\[18=gt\quad\Rightarrow\quad t=\frac{18}g=1.84\,\mathrm s.\]
Horizontal velocity is 6. At \(A\), vertical velocity:\[12-gt=12-18=-6.\]Thus\[V=\sqrt{6^2+(-6)^2}=\sqrt{72}=6\sqrt2\]\[=8.49\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}.\]
At the other point with this speed, vertical velocity is \(+6\):\[12-gt=6\]\[\Rightarrow t=\frac6g=0.61\,\mathrm s.\]

transcription.tex: 3. A ball is projected from \(A\) atop a cliff, position \(25\mathbf j\,\mathrm m\) relative to base \(O\) at sea level. Initial velocity is \((3p\mathbf i+p\mathbf j)\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), with constant \(p\). After 2 seconds it passes \(B\), position \((q\mathbf i+10\mathbf j)\,\mathrm m\), then hits the sea at \(C\). Model the ball as a particle moving freely under gravity and the sea as horizontal. Find velocity at \(B\).

\(\mathbf u=3p\mathbf i+p\mathbf j,\ \mathbf a=-9.8\mathbf j,\ t=2\).\[\mathbf v=\mathbf u+\mathbf at\]\[=\binom{3p}p+2\binom0{-9.8}=\binom{3p}{p-19.6}.\quad(1)\]Also, \(\mathbf r_0=25\mathbf j\), \(\mathbf r=q\mathbf i+10\mathbf j\):\[\mathbf s=\mathbf r-\mathbf r_0\]\[=q\mathbf i+10\mathbf j-25\mathbf j=q\mathbf i-15\mathbf j.\]

\[\mathbf s=\mathbf ut+\tfrac12\mathbf at^2\]\[\binom q{-15}=2\binom{3p}p+\frac{2^2}2\binom0{-9.8}.\]Compare vertical components:\[-15=2p-19.6\]\[2p=19.6-15\quad\Rightarrow\quad p=\frac{4.6}2=2.3.\]Substitute in (1):\[\mathbf v=\binom{3\times2.3}{2.3-19.6}=\binom{6.9}{-17.3}.\]Velocity at \(B\) is \((6.9\mathbf i-17\mathbf j)\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), components to 2 s.f.

transcription.tex: 4. A particle \(P\) is projected from \(O\) on horizontal ground with velocity \((3u\mathbf i+4u\mathbf j)\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). It lands 750 m from \(O\). (a) Show \(u=17.5\). (b) Find greatest height. (c) Find the angle its direction of motion makes with \(\mathbf i\) when \(t=5\,\mathrm s\).

\(\mathbf u=3u\mathbf i+4u\mathbf j,\ \mathbf a=-9.8\mathbf j,\ \mathbf s=750\mathbf i\).\[\mathbf s=\mathbf ut+\tfrac12\mathbf at^2\]\[750\mathbf i=(3u\mathbf i+4u\mathbf j)t+\tfrac12(-9.8\mathbf j)t^2\]\[=3ut\mathbf i+(4ut-4.9t^2)\mathbf j.\]Horizontal components:\[750=3ut\Rightarrow t=\frac{250}u.\]Vertical components:\[0=4ut-4.9t^2\]\[0=\frac{4u\times250}u-4.9\left(\frac{250}u\right)^2\]\[=1000-\frac{306250}{u^2}\]\[u^2=\frac{306250}{1000}=306.25\]\[u=\sqrt{306.25}=17.5.\]
At greatest height, vertical velocity is zero. Vertically, \(u_y=4u=70\), \(a=-9.8\), \(v_y=0\).\[v_y^2=u_y^2+2as\]\[0=70^2-2(9.8)s\]\[s=\frac{70^2}{2\times9.8}=250\,\mathrm m.\]

At \(t=5\),\[\mathbf v=\mathbf u+\mathbf at\]\[=(52.5\mathbf i+70\mathbf j)-5(9.8\mathbf j)\]\[=52.5\mathbf i+21\mathbf j.\]\[\tan\theta=\frac{v_y}{v_x}=\frac{21}{52.5}=0.4\]\[\theta=21.8^\circ\approx22^\circ\quad(2\text{ s.f.}),\]above the horizontal.

transcription.tex: 5. A particle is projected from \(O\) atop a cliff with velocity \((8\mathbf i+10\mathbf j)\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Moving freely under gravity, it strikes the sea at \(S\) after 6 seconds. Find (a) horizontal distance \(OS\); (b) vertical distance \(OS\). At time \(T\), velocity is \((8\mathbf i-14.5\mathbf j)\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). (c) Find \(T\) and position relative to \(O\).
Let position of \(S\) be \(x\mathbf i+y\mathbf j\). Horizontal motion:\[x=u_xt=8\times6=48\,\mathrm m.\]
Vertical motion:\[y=u_yt+\tfrac12at^2\]\[=10\times6-4.9\times6^2=-116.4\,\mathrm m.\]The vertical distance is 120 m (2 s.f.), downwards.

\[\mathbf v=\mathbf u+\mathbf aT\]\[8\mathbf i-14.5\mathbf j=(8\mathbf i+10\mathbf j)-9.8T\mathbf j.\]Compare vertical components:\[-14.5=10-9.8T\]\[T=\frac{24.5}{9.8}=\frac52=2.5\,\mathrm s.\]Then\[\mathbf s=\mathbf uT+\tfrac12\mathbf aT^2\]\[=\tfrac52(8\mathbf i+10\mathbf j)+\tfrac12(-9.8\mathbf j)(\tfrac52)^2\]\[=(8\times\tfrac52)\mathbf i+\left(10\times\tfrac52-4.9(\tfrac52)^2\right)\mathbf j\]\[=\left(20\mathbf i-\frac{45}8\mathbf j\right)\,\mathrm m.\]

transcription.tex: 6. Use \(g=10\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\). A body \(B\) is projected from \(O\) on horizontal ground with velocity \((a\mathbf i+b\mathbf j)\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), where \(a,b>0\). It moves freely under gravity until landing at \(P\), immediately coming to rest. Its position on the path is \((x\mathbf i+y\mathbf j)\,\mathrm m\).\par (a) Show \(y=bx/a-5x^2/a^2\).\par (b) Given \(a=8\), range \(OP=X\) and maximum height \(Y\), find (i) \(X\), (ii) \(Y\), in terms of \(b\).

\[\mathbf s=\mathbf ut+\tfrac12\mathbf at^2\]\[x\mathbf i+y\mathbf j=(a\mathbf i+b\mathbf j)t+\tfrac12(-10\mathbf j)t^2.\]Horizontal components:\[x=at\Rightarrow t=\frac xa.\quad(1)\]Vertical components:\[y=bt-5t^2.\quad(2)\]Substitute (1) in (2):\[y=\frac{bx}a-\frac{5x^2}{a^2},\]as required.
At landing, \(x=X,y=0,a=8\):\[0=\frac{bX}8-\frac{5X^2}{64}\]\[\frac{5X^2}{64}=\frac{bX}8\Rightarrow5X^2=8bX.\]Reject \(X=0\):\[X=\frac{8b}5=1.6b.\]
Maximum height occurs halfway along the range:\[x=\frac X2=\frac{4b}5.\]\[Y=\frac{b\times4b}{8\times5}-\frac{5(4b)^2}{64\times5^2}\]\[=\frac{b^2}{10}-\frac{b^2}{20}=\frac{b^2}{20}=0.05b^2.\]

transcription.tex: \[s\ \xrightarrow{\ d/dt\ }\ v\ \xrightarrow{\ d/dt\ }\ a\]\[s\ \xleftarrow{\ \int v\,dt\ }\ v\ \xleftarrow{\ \int a\,dt\ }\ a\]

In Mechanics Year 1, velocity is rate of change of displacement and acceleration is rate of change of velocity:\[v=\frac{ds}{dt},\qquad a=\frac{dv}{dt}.\]Reverse by integration: \(v=\int a\,dt\), \(s=\int v\,dt\), with constants found from initial conditions. Stay in one dimension, now using more complex Pure Year 2 functions.

A particle moving in a straight line has\[a=\cos(2\pi t)\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}},\quad t\geq0.\]At \(t=0\), \(v=1/(2\pi)\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Find (a) \(v(t)\); (b) maximum speed; (c) distance travelled in the first 3 seconds.
\[v=\int\cos(2\pi t)\,dt\]\[=\frac1{2\pi}\sin(2\pi t)+c.\]Reverse chain rule: divide by the constant multiplying \(t\). At \(t=0\):\[v=0+c=\frac1{2\pi}.\]\[v=\frac1{2\pi}\bigl(\sin(2\pi t)+1\bigr).\]
Maximum sine value is 1:\[v_{\max}=\frac1{2\pi}+\frac1{2\pi}=\frac1\pi\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}.\]Velocity is nonnegative, so this is also maximum speed.

Area under the velocity–time graph gives distance because \(v\geq0\). Factor out \(1/(2\pi)\):\[s=\frac1{2\pi}\int_0^3(\sin(2\pi t)+1)\,dt\]\[=\frac1{2\pi}\left[-\frac1{2\pi}\cos(2\pi t)+t\right]_0^3\]\[=\frac3{2\pi}=0.477\,\mathrm m\quad(3\text{ s.f.}).\]

transcription.tex: 7. A particle moves in a straight line with acceleration \(3\sqrt t\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\), \(t>0\), measured from when it begins motion. After 1 second, velocity is 2 m/s. Find the time taken to travel 16 m.

Integrate twice to obtain displacement, then find when 16 m has been travelled.\[v=\int a\,dt=\int3\sqrt t\,dt\]\[=3\times\frac23t^{3/2}+c=2t^{3/2}+c.\]Use \(t=1,v=2\):\[2=2(1^{3/2})+c\Rightarrow c=0.\]\[v=2t^{3/2}.\]

\[s=\int v\,dt=\int2t^{3/2}\,dt\]\[=\frac25\times2t^{5/2}+c_2=\frac45t^{5/2}+c_2.\]Measure displacement from the starting position, so \(s(0)=0\) gives \(c_2=0\). Since \(v\geq0\), distance equals displacement:\[16=\frac45t^{5/2}\]\[20=t^{5/2}\Rightarrow t=20^{2/5}=3.3144\ldots.\]It takes \(3.31\,\mathrm s\) (3 s.f.).
